newsitem.title: CANADA: Chrysler labor deal limits choice of suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler labor deal limits choice of suppliers.

text.p: Chrysler Corp of Canada Ltd's new deal with the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) lets the union play a role in the automaker's decisions to choose parts suppliers, contract provisions obtained by Reuters show.
In the language of the tentative labor agreement, Chrysler Corp's Canadian unit is obliged to follow a list of three considerations in selecting parts suppliers.
The side letter attached to the contract stipulates:
"* The company (Chrysler) expects suppliers to have responsible labor relations.
* The company believes that while the decision to join a union is an individual one, it is a decision that must be made without company intimidation, interference or risk of reprisal.
* The union may from time to time, raise concerns about the relationship with certain suppliers. The company commits to taking these concerns seriously."
Officials at the Canadian subsidiaries of General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co declined to comment on the agreement on suppliers.
